title: The Book of Nahum Timeline
sub: The Fall of Nineveh · No Relief for Your Fracture
desc: A single sustained oracle celebrating the coming destruction of Nineveh, the same city Jonah once saw spared — a jealous and avenging God finally brings the brutal Assyrian empire's cruelty to an irreversible end.

eras.label: Era One · Nahum 1
eras.name: A Zealous and Avenging God — Judgment on the Plotter Against the LORD
eras.dates: An oracle establishes the LORD's character before naming the specific enemy the book is written against

events.title: The Oracle of Nineveh — Slow to Anger, Great in Power
events.detail: The oracle describes the LORD as both zealous and avenging toward his foes, yet a fortress for those who seek refuge in him, his power shown in cosmic upheaval — mountains trembling, seas dried up by a shout.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] is slow to anger but great in power; the LORD [Yahweh] will certainly not allow the wicked to go unpunished.”

events.title: A Wicked Military Strategist Who Plots Against the LORD
events.detail: The LORD promises complete destruction of whoever plots against him, breaking Assyria's yoke bar off Judah and issuing a decree of doom against the strategist who devised evil — widely understood as the Assyrian king.

verses.text: “Whatever you plot against the LORD [Yahweh], he will completely destroy! Distress will not arise a second time.”

eras.label: Era Two · Nahum 2
eras.name: Good News for Judah — the Fall of Nineveh Described
eras.dates: A herald announces peace to Judah just before the chapter turns to a vivid battle-scene of Nineveh's destruction. (The Hebrew text's chapter division falls one verse earlier than most English translations: the herald's announcement, numbered as the close of chapter 1 in most English Bibles, opens chapter 2 in the Hebrew numbering used here, shifting every following verse number in this chapter up by one — a versification difference only, not a different event. NET itself marks this inline as “(2:1)” and “(2:2)”.)

events.title: Look! A Herald Is Running on the Mountains!
events.detail: A herald's feet on the mountains announce deliverance to Judah, calling the nation to celebrate its sacred festivals now that the threat from the wicked Assyrians is permanently cut off. (Numbered 1:15 in most English translations; the Hebrew text used here opens chapter 2 with this verse instead.)

verses.text: “Look! A herald is running on the mountains! A messenger is proclaiming deliverance: ‘Celebrate your sacred festivals, O Judah! Fulfill your sacred vows.’”

events.title: Destruction, Devastation, and Desolation — Nineveh's Fall
events.detail: A rapid, cinematic battle scene depicts chariots racing madly and Nineveh's defenses collapsing, the once-mighty lion's den now stripped of its plunder and its people fleeing in terror.

verses.text: “I am against you!” declares the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies. “I will burn your chariots with fire… the voices of your messengers will no longer be heard.”

eras.label: Era Three · Nahum 3
eras.name: Woe to the City of Bloodshed — No Relief for Your Fracture
eras.dates: A closing woe oracle exposes Nineveh's violent history and predatory economy before pronouncing its ruin as final and irreversible

events.title: Woe to the City Guilty of Bloodshed — a Wanton Prostitute
events.detail: Nineveh is denounced as a city guilty of bloodshed and lies whose violent conquests and exploitative alliances are compared to a prostitute's sorceries, about to be publicly disgraced before the nations she once dominated.

verses.text: “Woe to the city guilty of bloodshed! She is full of lies; she is filled with plunder; she has hoarded her spoil!”

events.title: No Relief for Your Fracture — Your Demise Is Like a Fatal Injury
events.detail: Even mighty Thebes fell despite its defenses, and Nineveh will fare no better; the book closes with the announcement that Assyria's wound is incurable and the whole world will clap in relief at its downfall.

verses.text: “Your destruction is like an incurable wound; your demise is like a fatal injury. All who hear what has happened to you will clap their hands for joy.”
